To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differential rotation in the bulk of a convective shell in a rapidly rotating star is described by a single characteristic, and that the differential rotation of the bulk of a rapidly rotating convective shell in the presence of a tachocline and a radiative core is described by a pair of characteristics.

the differential rotation of the Sun is a direct consequence of the thermal wind balance equation and the narrow convective shell, and that the isorotation profiles in the bulk of both the SC and the tacholcline can be described by the characteristics of the thermal wind equation.

the isorotation surface contours in the bulk and the tacholine can be deduced from a simple set of equations, and the form of the contours is identical to the characteristics of the thermal wind equation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical properties of the thermal wind equation in the presence of a thin convective layer.
the dynamics of the SCZ as a whole and not just the tachoclinic region.
the mathematical properties of the TWE, the nature of conduction in a convective shell, and the consequences of combining the two.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TWE is a powerful tool for describing the rotational behaviour of the SCZ.

the differential rotation of the SCZ can be understood as an approximate solution of thermal wind balance, and that the same is true of the tachoclines, but that the latter are more complicated than the former.

the isorotation surface in the bulk of SCZ is a characteristic of the thermal wind equation, and the tacholine contours are also determined by the TWE, but with a different functional form for the residual entropy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TWE is the key to understanding differential rotation in the SCZ, while the nature of the tachoclines is a separate problem.

the isorotation contour shapes of the Sun’s interior can be understood in terms of a single equation, the TWE, which can be combined with a simple model of convection to yield a global model of the Sun’s rotation.
the thermal wind balance is a necessary condition for the existence of the isorotations contours in the bulk SCZ, and that they can be described by a narrow convective layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple mathematical model can be constructed to explain the shape of the constant angular velocity contours, and that the model is consistent with the physics of convection and thermal wind balance.
a narrow convective zone in the bulk of a rotating convective envelope is sufficient to explain the observed rotation profiles.
the isorotation surface in the bulk of SCZ is a characteristic of the equation of thermal-wind balance.
